You write internal pages for the SRE team of Sorrel. Write ONE page in Markdown, plain and realistic,
the way a small, busy SRE team writes: specific, a little dry, short sections, bullets where they help, no marketing
tone, no summary of what the page is for. Length: about 450 words.

Start with exactly the header lines you are given, unchanged. Then write the body.

Hard rules:
- Use every fact you are given, with every number, name, code, config key and date exactly as written. Add no new
  facts: no new incidents, numbers, error codes, config keys, partner names or people. You may add connecting words,
  a one-line judgement from the author, and a routine sign-off.
- Keep the team's own words for things exactly as the facts give them; do not explain a term in other words and do not
  add a plain-language gloss.
- An error code (like ABC-1234) appears only where a fact puts it, written in passing inside a sentence. Never put an
  error code in a heading, a table header or the first line of a section.
- Never give rollback steps or rollback commands for any service. Never mention a tool called dtool. Mention Shipyard
  only if a fact does, and then only as the fact says, with no commands.
- No phone numbers, account ids, email addresses or URLs. Do not mention on-call pay, allowances or contracts.
- Do not copy alert rules or thresholds into tables, and do not write lists of 'for this alert, the first move is X'.
- Everything in the page happens on or before the page's date.

What the team works with:
Sorrel is a scheduling app (salons, clinics, tutors book appointments through it). Four services: web
(pages and the admin tool), api (businesses, bookings, search, the partner API, the audit log), payments (charges,
refunds, weekly payouts to businesses), notifier (email and SMS). Regions: ap-northeast, us-east, eu-west.
Owners: Aiko (web), Ravi (api), Mei (payments), Tom (notifier). Others: Kenji Sato (platform lead), Sara (platform
engineer), Hana (support lead), Daniel (api engineer), Yuki (notifier engineer), Priya (web engineer), Leo (payments
engineer), Noor (SRE, joined the rotation in April 2026). Providers: stripe (cards), twilio (SMS), sendgrid (email),
cloudflare (CDN and firewall), aws (hosting). The incident channel is #inc-live; boards are "Sorrel / web",
"Sorrel / api", "Sorrel / payments", "Sorrel / notifier"; logs are searched in sorrel-prod-*; people use the paging
tool, the metrics tool, the log search tool and the deploy tool. Severities: P1, P2, P3. A handover is finished when
the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

The five actions on-call chooses from:
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

# On-call handover, week of 2025-10-20

Date: 2025-10-20  
Owner: Yuki (notifier), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Daniel (api)  

### Shift summary

Fairly quiet rotation overall, though Tuesday had a couple of provider bumps and an unresolved checkout issue to keep track of.

### Provider alerts

* Tuesday 2025-10-14: notifier-sms-fail fired for 7 minutes. The twilio status page listed a carrier incident in Japan, and delivery recovered on its own. First move: check provider.
* Tuesday 2025-10-14: web-cdn-edge reached 2.6 % for 6 minutes. The cloudflare status page showed an incident at one edge location. First move: check provider.

### Ongoing issues

During the shift, PAY-4031 came back on Tuesday evening: the acquirer timed out on the 3-D Secure challenge and 41 checkouts failed in about 25 minutes. The checkout waits 10 s for the 3-D Secure answer. Leo opened a ticket; no change yet. Keep an eye on payments if this surfaces again before the ticket gets an update.

### Operational notes

Quirk: the log search tool's default time window is the last 15 minutes; widen it before deciding there are no errors.

Sign-off: Handing over to Daniel. Please acknowledge and mark taken in #inc-live.

# On-call handover, week of 2025-10-20

Date: 2025-10-20  
Owner: Yuki (notifier), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Daniel (api)  

## 1. Shift summary

Shift was mostly manageable, though Tuesday brought a cluster of external dependencies misbehaving within a narrow window. Most of the noise cleared without engineering intervention, but we saw repeat failures on payment challenges that need ongoing attention. No internal rollbacks were required this week, and general traffic across our core scheduling flows stayed healthy.

## 2. What happened

A few specific events occurred during the shift that required paging triage and provider monitoring:

- PAY-4031 came back on Tuesday evening: the acquirer timed out on the 3-D Secure challenge and 41 checkouts failed in about 25 minutes. The checkout waits 10 s for the 3-D Secure answer. Leo opened a ticket; no change yet. We monitored the error budget and kept watch on the payments board, but because the bottleneck sat upstream with the acquirer, we waited on their confirmation rather than touching the service.
- notifier-sms-fail fired for 7 minutes on Tuesday 2025-10-14; the twilio status page listed a carrier incident in Japan; delivery recovered on its own. First move: check provider. In this case, looking at the third-party status dashboard confirmed the carrier fault immediately, so we took no internal action while messages cleared.
- web-cdn-edge reached 2.6 % for 6 minutes on Tuesday 2025-10-14; the cloudflare status page showed an incident at one edge location. First move: check provider. Traffic re-routed cleanly once their edge popped back online, bringing edge error rates back down to baseline without further impact to salon or clinic booking flows.

## 3. Service status

- web: Normal, apart from the brief elevation in edge errors linked to the cloudflare incident noted above.
- api: Normal throughout the entire shift with steady background latency.
- payments: Impacted on Tuesday evening due to the 3-D Secure timeouts described above; currently waiting on provider progress via Leo's ticket.
- notifier: Normal, following the short-lived SMS carrier delivery spike on Tuesday.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

Keep an eye out when searching logs during triage this week. Quirk: the log search tool's default time window is the last 15 minutes; widen it before deciding there are no errors. When tracking short-lived spikes or paging alerts that fired slightly outside that fifteen-minute scope, expanding the search interval in the log search tool prevents false negatives.

For payments, check in with Leo if repeat bursts of checkout challenge failures appear in the logs. If you spot new acquirer drops, verify whether the ticket has updates before escalating further. Other than that, third-party provider dashboards should remain your initial stop if notifier or CDN edge metrics blink again.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over primary rotation duties now. Daniel, please post in #inc-live to take the shift when you are ready.

— Yuki

# On-call handover, week of 2025-10-06

Last updated: 2025-10-06 10:00 JST  
Owner: Priya (web), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Leo (payments)  

## 1. Shift summary

The shift was mostly quiet, with only two alerts needing attention across the week. Outside dependencies caused brief noise on Friday evening, but internal systems held up without manual rollbacks or service restarts. The platform ran steadily across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west, leaving the boards in good shape for the coming rotation.

## 2. What happened

On Thursday 2025-10-02 at 10:47 JST, api-partner-reject fired for one partner. The author used the log search tool to search sorrel-prod-* and review what api had rejected. The partner ran a full re-sync and hit its contracted limit. Following the team guidelines, the first move was: read logs. Once the nature of the burst was clear from the logs, the author checked in with Ravi. Ravi confirmed the limit stays as it is. No configuration changes were made and no further rejections were observed once their sync finished.

On Friday 2025-10-03 at 20:41 JST, payments-provider-timeout fired. Because the alert already pointed at an outside dependency, the first move was: check provider. The author looked at external dashboards, and the stripe status page reported degraded API performance. The issue cleared in 24 minutes without requiring internal intervention, and checkout operations returned to nominal latency across all active regions. The author logged the timeline in #inc-live and kept monitoring until the alert resolved on its own.

## 3. Service status

- web: Normal throughout the entire rotation, with steady traffic and clean metrics across all customer facing pages and the admin tool.
- api: Pointing back to what happened on Thursday 2025-10-02, when the partner re-sync caused rate limits to trip; otherwise normal.
- payments: Pointing back to what happened on Friday 2025-10-03 during the upstream Stripe degradation; otherwise normal.
- notifier: Normal all week across email and SMS delivery paths with SendGrid and Twilio.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- Reminder for incoming: no deploys after 16:00 JST on Friday or between 22:00 and 07:00 JST, except rollbacks and fixes for open P1s.
- Keep an eye on "Sorrel / payments" and "Sorrel / api" on the boards at the start of your shift to confirm downstream queues remain drained following normal weekend traffic.
- If third-party metrics look anomalous in the paging tool or metrics tool, verify external vendor status before digging into local containers or queue backlogs.
- When an alert trips on contracted thresholds, remember to check with Ravi before considering any quota adjustments for partner sync jobs.
- Post any P1, P2, or P3 updates directly in #inc-live so Hana and the rest of the team have visibility on customer impact.

## 5. Sign-off

The rotation is ready to transfer over. Please review the boards and post "taken" in #inc-live once you have reviewed this log and assumed primary coverage. Have a safe shift.

Handing over primary duty now. The shift passes to Yuki once acknowledged with "taken" in #inc-live.

# On-call handover, week of 2025-10-27

Last updated: 2025-10-27 10:00 JST  
Owner: Daniel (api), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Sara (platform)  

## 1. Shift summary

The shift was mostly quiet with zero P1 or P2 events and minimal customer friction throughout the week. Web had two brief alerts over the weekend that were handled cleanly without customer reports or wider fallout. Api, payments, and notifier ran steadily with no incidents or alerts to report.

## 2. What happened

The following items came up across the shift:

* WEB-5106 on business logo uploads over 10 MB: working as designed (the limit is 10 MB). Support already has a help article; nothing to do. I reviewed this when a question came in from the team. Because this is the intended system boundary and customer guidance is already published, no platform changes were needed and my decision was no action.

* web-4xx at 1.2 % for 12 minutes on Saturday 2025-10-25: an old marketing link pointing at a removed page. First move: read logs; no customer reports; ticket filed. The elevated rate did not cause broken core appointment workflows or trigger client support escalations. After looking through the paths in the log search tool to confirm it was strictly external traffic hitting a dead route, I closed the alert response and filed the tracking card for web to clean up redirects or retire the stale asset link as needed.

* web-node-restart fired on Saturday 2025-10-25 for one us-east web node (two restarts in 30 minutes, out of memory); the node was replaced. First move: read logs. The rest of the pool absorbed the requests without elevated latency or dropped traffic. After confirming the process memory exhaustion pattern on that specific instance, the node was swapped out. Capacity returned to baseline and us-east remained stable for the remainder of the weekend.

## 3. Service status

* web: Normal, after resolving the dead marketing route 4xx blip and replacing the single restarted us-east node.
* api: Normal.
* payments: Normal.
* notifier: Normal.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

A few items to keep in mind as Sara takes over:

* The incoming on-call confirmed access to the paging tool, the metrics tool, log search and the deploy tool before taking the shift.
* Keep an eye on us-east web host memory in the metrics tool just to verify the replacement instance behaves identically to the rest of the cluster during peak appointment booking hours.
* The ticket filed for the stale marketing link from Saturday 2025-10-25 is sitting with web, so no immediate on-call intervention is expected unless traffic surges again.
* If logo upload queries come up again from Hana's team, confirm whether the payload exceeded the 10 MB limit before digging into deeper service telemetry.
* Remember the handover is finished when the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the primary rotation to Sara. Thanks all for the quiet week.

— Daniel

Author: Sara (platform), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Priya (web)  

## 1. Shift summary

A calm shift overall with routine seasonal checks and no major customer impact across our regions. Most of the time went into verifying past fixes and watching partner traffic spikes. Everything remained steady through the weekend, leaving production in a solid state for the incoming rotation.

- **Partner rate limit event**: On Wednesday 2025-10-29 at 10:54 JST, the `api-partner-reject` alert fired for one partner. Looking into the traffic, the partner ran a full re-sync and hit its contracted limit. I chose to read logs as the first move to confirm the rejection pattern and ensure the partner was receiving the standard payload rather than internal failures. After reviewing the pattern, Ravi confirmed the limit stays as it is. Because this was expected behavior under current contract terms, no further adjustments were made.

- **Payment timeout follow-up**: The PAY-4031 follow-up from two weeks ago is done: on Thursday Leo raised the 3-D Secure wait from 10 s to 25 s. We monitored traffic on payments across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west following the adjustment, and PAY-4031 has not come back since. Card verification flows have remained smooth through the weekend.

- **Daylight saving time verification**: The US clock change on Sunday 2025-11-02 went clean this year. Daniel checked 212 bookings at us-east businesses for the days around the change and every one showed the right time. No customer reports came through support, and booking creation rates remained aligned with normal weekend baselines.

## 3. Service status

- **web**: Normal; no alerts fired and page rendering metrics were flat throughout the week.
- **api**: Normal; partner rejections on Wednesday were limited to the single partner that hit its contracted limit, as noted in what happened.
- **payments**: Normal; card flows are healthy following Thursday's adjustment to the 3-D Secure wait.
- **notifier**: Normal; message delivery queues remained clear across email and SMS with no anomalies.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- Quirk: the log search tool's default time window is the last 15 minutes; widen it before deciding there are no errors. This caught me briefly during the partner re-sync review on Wednesday when checking older request traces in sorrel-prod-*.

- The payments adjustment from Leo is holding well, but keep an eye on gateway latency if upstream traffic rises during business payouts.
- Handover concludes as usual once you ack this page and post to the incident channel.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the rotation to Priya now. Please write "taken" in #inc-live to complete the handover.

- notifier: normal; email processing delays on Thursday traced directly to sendgrid.

- Keep an eye on ap-northeast metrics during the early morning hours (02:50 to 03:30 JST) to verify the replica change holds up under weekday loads, even though Daniel's adjustment kept Friday night completely clean.

parts.text:
You write internal pages for the SRE team of Sorrel. Write ONE page in Markdown, plain and realistic,
the way a small, busy SRE team writes: specific, a little dry, short sections, bullets where they help, no marketing
tone, no summary of what the page is for. Length: 550 to 700 words; do not stop short.
Sections, in this order, with numbered '## ' headings in the house style ('## 1. Shift summary'):
shift summary (two or three sentences, the author's view of the week); what happened (each fact, with the author's
plain account of what was seen and done); a one-line-per-service status for web, api, payments and notifier (normal,
or pointing back to what happened; no new numbers); notes for the incoming on-call; sign-off.

Start with exactly the header lines you are given, unchanged. Then write the body.

Hard rules:
- Use every fact you are given, with every number, name, code, config key and date exactly as written. Add no new
  facts: no new incidents, numbers, error codes, config keys, partner names or people. You may add connecting words,
  a one-line judgement from the author, and a routine sign-off.
- Keep the team's own words for things exactly as the facts give them; do not explain a term in other words and do not
  add a plain-language gloss.
- An error code (like ABC-1234) appears only where a fact puts it, written in passing inside a sentence. Never put an
  error code in a heading, a table header or the first line of a section.
- Never give rollback steps or rollback commands for any service. Never mention a tool called dtool. Mention Shipyard
  only if a fact does, and then only as the fact says, with no commands.
- No phone numbers, account ids, email addresses or URLs. Do not mention on-call pay, allowances or contracts.
- Do not copy alert rules or thresholds into tables, and do not write lists of 'for this alert, the first move is X'.
- Everything in the page happens on or before the page's date.

What the team works with:
Sorrel is a scheduling app (salons, clinics, tutors book appointments through it). Four services: web
(pages and the admin tool), api (businesses, bookings, search, the partner API, the audit log), payments (charges,
refunds, weekly payouts to businesses), notifier (email and SMS). Regions: ap-northeast, us-east, eu-west.
Owners: Aiko (web), Ravi (api), Mei (payments), Tom (notifier). Others: Kenji Sato (platform lead), Sara (platform
engineer), Hana (support lead), Daniel (api engineer), Yuki (notifier engineer), Priya (web engineer), Leo (payments
engineer), Noor (SRE, joined the rotation in April 2026). Providers: stripe (cards), twilio (SMS), sendgrid (email),
cloudflare (CDN and firewall), aws (hosting). The incident channel is #inc-live; boards are "Sorrel / web",
"Sorrel / api", "Sorrel / payments", "Sorrel / notifier"; logs are searched in sorrel-prod-*; people use the paging
tool, the metrics tool, the log search tool and the deploy tool. Severities: P1, P2, P3. A handover is finished when
the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

The five actions on-call chooses from:
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

# On-call handover, week of 2025-12-08

Date: 2025-12-08  
Author: Priya (web), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Daniel (api)  

## 1. Shift summary

A fairly quiet week overall with no major customer disruption or paging emergencies. Most production noise was isolated to the web tier, specifically one bad node recycling under memory pressure and a brief spike in client errors caused by obsolete external links. The rest of the platform ran quietly without needing out-of-hours intervention.

## 2. What happened

A couple of events hit the rota across the week, both on the web service:

* On Friday 2025-12-05, the `web-node-restart` alert fired for one us-east web node after it experienced two restarts in 30 minutes, running out of memory. First move: read logs. I went into the log search tool to inspect what the instance was handling prior to termination. Following the inspection, the node was replaced, and capacity returned to normal stability in us-east without further memory exhaustion.

* On Saturday 2025-12-06, `web-4xx` ran at 1.9 % for 12 minutes. First move: read logs. Looking through sorrel-prod-* output showed incoming traffic hitting an old marketing link pointing at a removed page. There were no customer reports received by Hana or support, and a ticket was filed to clean up or redirect the legacy path.

## 3. Service status

* **web**: Recovered and stable; see notes above on the us-east node replacement on Friday 2025-12-05 and the brief 4xx blip on Saturday 2025-12-06.
* **api**: Normal throughout the rotation; no alerts or unhandled exceptions logged.
* **payments**: Normal; weekly payouts and routine charge processing completed cleanly.
* **notifier**: Normal; message delivery remained green across all regions.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

* Quirk: the queue depth panel on the "Sorrel / notifier" board lags the delivered-per-minute panel by about 2 minutes; read both before deciding.
* If you see any trailing 404s on web paths, check the ticket filed from Saturday before treating it as an application-level regression.
* Keep an eye on memory usage across the remaining us-east web instances in the metrics tool just in case the node failure on Friday was part of a slower leak pattern.
* Remember to announce handover completion as usual once you have reviewed the active boards and verified the paging tool.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over to Daniel. A handover is finished when the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live. Thanks all, have a good shift.

— Priya

Last updated: 2025-12-15 10:00 JST  
Author: Daniel (api), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Sara (platform)  

## 1. Shift summary

The rotation this week was mostly quiet, punctuated only by brief upstream provider blips and expected validation chatter on the partner endpoints. Core application components and data stores behaved normally across all three regions without any internal service degradations. The few pages received resolved without needing intervention beyond confirming external status boards and tracking recovery.

## 2. What happened

* On Wednesday 2025-12-10, notifier-sms-fail fired for 7 minutes. The twilio status page listed a carrier incident in Japan, and delivery recovered on its own. First move: check provider. We monitored the outgoing queues in ap-northeast until the numbers normalized without needing manual retries.
* Outside of those alerts, we saw API-2210 rejections for one partner all week: they sent bookings for slots outside the business's opening hours. That is the check doing its job; Ravi told the partner. The rejections caused some predictable noise on the partner route graphs, but they represent expected validation behavior rather than an api regression, so no platform adjustments were necessary.

## 3. Service status

* web: Normal, apart from the brief 6-minute web-cdn-edge incident on Tuesday 2025-12-09.
* api: Normal; the validation rejections throughout the week were expected traffic handling.
* payments: Normal throughout the shift.
* notifier: Normal, following the 7-minute notifier-sms-fail blip on Wednesday 2025-12-10.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

* Quirk: the queue depth panel on the "Sorrel / notifier" board lags the delivered-per-minute panel by about 2 minutes; read both before deciding. If notifier alerts pop up, give both panels a joint review before assuming messages are backing up.

* Ensure you post in #inc-live to confirm the shift transfer once you have reviewed the active dashboards.

Handing over the primary pager to Sara. Handover is finished when Sara writes "taken" in #inc-live.

You write internal pages for the SRE team of Sorrel. Write ONE page in Markdown, plain and realistic,
the way a small, busy SRE team writes: specific, a little dry, short sections, bullets where they help, no marketing
tone, no summary of what the page is for. Length: 550 to 700 words; do not stop short.
Sections, in this order, with numbered '## ' headings in the house style ('## 1. Shift summary'):
shift summary (two or three sentences, the author's view of the week); what happened (each fact, with the author's
plain account of what was seen and done); a one-line-per-service status for web, api, payments and notifier (normal,
or pointing back to what happened; no new numbers); notes for the incoming on-call; sign-off.

Start with exactly the header lines you are given, unchanged. Then write the body.

Hard rules:
- Use every fact you are given, with every number, name, code, config key and date exactly as written. Add no new
  facts: no new incidents, numbers, error codes, config keys, partner names or people. You may add connecting words,
  a one-line judgement from the author, and a routine sign-off.
- Keep the team's own words for things exactly as the facts give them; do not explain a term in other words and do not
  add a plain-language gloss.
- An error code (like ABC-1234) appears only where a fact puts it, written in passing inside a sentence. Never put an
  error code in a heading, a table header or the first line of a section.
- Never give rollback steps or rollback commands for any service. Never mention a tool called dtool. Mention Shipyard
  only if a fact does, and then only as the fact says, with no commands.
- No phone numbers, account ids, email addresses or URLs. Do not mention on-call pay, allowances or contracts.
- Do not copy alert rules or thresholds into tables, and do not write lists of 'for this alert, the first move is X'.
- Everything in the page happens on or before the page's date.

What the team works with:
Sorrel is a scheduling app (salons, clinics, tutors book appointments through it). Four services: web
(pages and the admin tool), api (businesses, bookings, search, the partner API, the audit log), payments (charges,
refunds, weekly payouts to businesses), notifier (email and SMS). Regions: ap-northeast, us-east, eu-west.
Owners: Aiko (web), Ravi (api), Mei (payments), Tom (notifier). Others: Kenji Sato (platform lead), Sara (platform
engineer), Hana (support lead), Daniel (api engineer), Yuki (notifier engineer), Priya (web engineer), Leo (payments
engineer), Noor (SRE, joined the rotation in April 2026). Providers: stripe (cards), twilio (SMS), sendgrid (email),
cloudflare (CDN and firewall), aws (hosting). The incident channel is #inc-live; boards are "Sorrel / web",
"Sorrel / api", "Sorrel / payments", "Sorrel / notifier"; logs are searched in sorrel-prod-*; people use the paging
tool, the metrics tool, the log search tool and the deploy tool. Severities: P1, P2, P3. A handover is finished when
the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

The five actions on-call chooses from:
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

Last updated: 2026-01-19 10:00 JST  
Owner: Daniel (api), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Sara (platform)  

## 1. Shift summary

The past week was quiet overall with no customer outages or pages outside normal hours. We had brief friction from an unoptimized database query during European traffic hours and some stale logs taking up capacity on a single host over the weekend. Both were dealt with quickly using standard steps and did not require paging owners or rolling back releases.

## 2. What happened

- On Thursday 2026-01-15, api-latency on the search endpoint group in eu-west reached 2.3 s p95 for 11 minutes during the Europe morning peak. The first move taken was to read logs. Looking through sorrel-prod-* logs showed one slow query that backed up the workers temporarily. Daniel opened a ticket on the Sorrel / api board for the api team to optimize the query execution path, and the latency settled on its own once peak traffic stabilized.
- On Saturday 2026-01-17, web-disk passed 80 % on one web node because of old log files accumulating on the root partition. The initial response was to read logs to confirm which paths were consuming space. Priya cleared the rotated logs in working hours, which brought disk usage back down well under warning levels without interrupting running processes.

## 3. Service status

- **web**: Normal after Priya cleared the rotated logs on the affected node.
- **api**: Normal, tracking the search endpoint group slow query ticket filed following the eu-west spike.
- **payments**: Normal throughout the shift.
- **notifier**: Normal throughout the shift.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- The incoming on-call confirmed access to the paging tool, the metrics tool, log search and the deploy tool before taking the shift.
- Keep an eye on the search endpoint group in eu-west during the Europe morning peak until the api team takes on the slow query ticket, just in case traffic spikes push latency back up.
- The web host that alerted on disk capacity has plenty of headroom now, but watch out for similar disk growth patterns across other hosts if log rotation gets stuck again.
- Standard reminder on incident workflow: use #inc-live for any coordination, pick the right first move from the five actions, and ensure severity is marked properly for any customer-facing degradation.

## 5. Sign-off

Handover review completed with Sara. Handing over rotation now; shift is complete once Sara posts taken in #inc-live.

Daniel (api)

Owner: Sara (platform), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Priya (web)  

## 1. Shift summary

The rotation this week was mostly quiet, broken up by an SMS rate-limit issue in the middle of the week and two alarms on the web tier. Both web alerts were handled cleanly without customer disruption, one needing an instance replacement and the other turning out to be harmless crawler traffic. Overall system health remains stable across all regions heading into the next shift.

## 2. What happened

The following items came up across the week:

- notifier.sms_batch_size went from 500 to 200 on Wednesday: twilio answered 429 (too many requests) during the nightly reminder batch when we sent 500 at a time. Looking through sorrel-prod-* output showed the memory footprint climbing steadily until the process supervisor stepped in. Once the node was replaced, memory utilization on the surviving instances in us-east settled back into expected boundaries and no further instability was observed.
- web-traffic fired on Friday 2026-01-23 at 14:54 JST: a search-engine crawler on public business pages, about 3.8x the same hour last week, all 2xx. First move: no action; ticket for Aiko about crawler limits. Because cloudflare handled the inbound requests without elevated latency and all responses returned successful status codes, we did not apply any edge blocks or manual rate-limiting during the spike. The ticket was filed on "Sorrel / web" so Aiko can review path-specific rate-limiting rules when convenient.

## 3. Service status

- web: Normal; recovered after the us-east node replacement on Thursday and the Friday crawler spike.
- api: Normal; no alerts fired and baseline metrics remained flat across all regions throughout the rotation.
- payments: Normal; card charges, refunds, and scheduled payouts completed without any intervention needed.
- notifier: Normal; running with the updated batch configuration following Wednesday's change.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- The incoming on-call confirmed access to the paging tool, the metrics tool, log search and the deploy tool before taking the shift.
- Keep an eye on the nightly reminder dispatches in notifier to verify the adjusted pacing continues to avoid provider backpressure. The extra run time has not caused delays with morning appointment deliveries, but Tom's team should be kept in the loop if any upstream schedules shift.
- Watch us-east web metrics following the node replacement from Thursday. While the replacement resolved the immediate alert, keep sorrel-prod-* in mind if any individual instances drift away from the fleet median.
- Aiko will look at the crawler ticket from Friday; no urgent platform work is pending there unless a similar volume spike begins to impact upstream response times.
- Routine reminder that any escalations belong in #inc-live.

## 5. Sign-off

Handover ready for Priya. Handover is finished when Priya writes "taken" in #inc-live.

— Sara

# On-call handover, week of 2026-02-02

Date: 2026-02-02  
Owner: Priya (web), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Leo (payments)  

## 1. Shift summary

A fairly manageable week with two brief alerts and a clean resolution on calendar latency. The fleet ran stably across regions overall, though we had one host-level blip in Tokyo and an external dependency hiccup on email deliveries. Outside of those items, routine background traffic stayed within normal bounds and operations proceeded smoothly.

## 2. What happened

- On Wednesday 2026-01-28, api-pool reached 94 % on one ap-northeast node for 10 minutes. The load balancer took the node out and it was replaced. First move: read logs. Checked the system output in sorrel-prod-* to see what pinned the workers before replacement; the replacement node came up healthy and pool utilization normalized immediately without further impact on the region.
- On Thursday 2026-01-29, notifier-email-fail touched 21 % for 6 minutes. The sendgrid status page showed delayed processing. First move: check provider. The issue sat entirely downstream with the mail partner, so we monitored queue posture while they recovered, and it cleared with nothing changed on our side.
- We investigated N+1 queries on the week-view calendar endpoint: for businesses with 40 or more staff, api fetched each staff member's bookings one query at a time, and the endpoint's p95 reached 6 s. Daniel batched the staff lookups into one query on Thursday; p95 is now about 700 ms. The fix was applied cleanly and endpoint latency has stayed flat since then.
- The Sunday payout job ran at 23:00 JST and finished in 36 minutes. The batch executed to completion without errors or stalls.

## 3. Service status

- web: Normal; traffic across public pages and the admin tool remained stable with no incidents during the shift.
- api: Normal; calendar latency improved following Daniel's batching fix, and pool usage stabilized after the node replacement in ap-northeast.
- payments: Normal; weekly payouts completed smoothly on Sunday night with no failed transfers or stuck jobs.
- notifier: Normal; delivery rates returned to expected levels after Thursday's external SendGrid processing delay.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- Keep an eye on "Sorrel / api" dashboards during the morning ramp-up in ap-northeast, specifically around connection pool utilization, to verify the replaced instance behavior remains steady.
- The week-view calendar endpoint has been quiet since Thursday's deploy, but watch p95 metrics for larger multi-staff clinics and salons on the metrics tool to confirm the batched query behavior holds up under heavier Monday booking traffic.
- Notifier outbound queues are empty and SendGrid processing times have remained clean over the weekend, but remember to verify third-party status dashboards before digging into local services if delivery percentages wobble.
- Payments pipelines are quiet following the Sunday payout completion; monitor standard refund and charge flows on "Sorrel / payments".
- Handover is complete once you acknowledge the shift and post "taken" in #inc-live.

## 5. Sign-off

Signed off by Priya (web) on 2026-02-02. Passing the primary rotation to Leo (payments). Have a quiet week.

# On-call handover, week of 2026-02-09

Date: 2026-02-09  
Author: Leo (payments), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Yuki (notifier)  

## 1. Shift summary

The rotation had three notable disruptions this week across hosting, edge networking, and third-party delivery. Most core processing remained steady, but two provider-side blips and an unexplained node provisioning fault on api required manual intervention and monitoring. The rest of the days were quiet, and payments ran through the regular cycles without any trouble.

## 2. What happened

On Wednesday, we observed API-2387 errors in eu-west following a node replacement. Traffic for search requests that landed on the new node failed with a missing search shard. Daniel was brought in and rebuilt the shard on that node (40 min). The root cause is not known yet, so we have kept the node under observation without making further environmental adjustments.

On Friday 2026-02-06, web-cdn-edge reached 2.5 % for 6 minutes. The cloudflare status page showed an incident at one edge location during that exact window. First move: check provider. The routing cleared up upstream without requiring configuration adjustments on the origins, and the elevated rate dropped back down on its own.

On Saturday 2026-02-07, notifier-email-fail touched 29 % for 6 minutes. The sendgrid status page showed delayed processing at the time. First move: check provider. It cleared with nothing changed on our side, and downstream delivery recovered cleanly once their queue backlog drained out.

## 3. Service status

- web: Pointing back to what happened with web-cdn-edge reaching 2.5 % during the cloudflare incident on Friday 2026-02-06, otherwise normal.
- api: Pointing back to what happened with missing search shard failures in eu-west after the Wednesday node replacement.
- payments: Normal across charges, refunds, and weekly payouts with no incidents seen.
- notifier: Pointing back to what happened with notifier-email-fail touching 29 % during the sendgrid delayed processing event on Saturday 2026-02-07.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

Keep an eye on regional search query logs in eu-west in case another node replacement gets triggered by hosting maintenance before Daniel closes the investigation. If a node cycles and throws shard faults again, Daniel already knows the rebuild process, though we still need to determine why provisioning left it absent in the first place.

Take note of a dashboard display issue when triaging delivery alerts this week. Quirk: the queue depth panel on the 'Sorrel / notifier' board lags the delivered-per-minute panel by about 2 minutes; read both before deciding. Relying on queue depth alone right after an edge or provider blip can give an inaccurate impression of whether a drain has stalled or is already making progress.

Outside of those items, the external provider dashboards should be your initial stop if customer edge drops or email spikes recur. As demonstrated on Friday and Saturday, brief spikes in external delivery or edge error rates can resolve entirely on the upstream end without manual intervention or configuration adjustments on our side.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the primary shift now. Please review the notes above, run through the open dashboards, and post "taken" in #inc-live once you are ready to take over the rotation for the coming week.

Leo

# On-call handover, week of 2026-02-23

Date: 2026-02-23  
Author: Daniel (api), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Sara (platform)  

## 1. Shift summary

The rotation this past week was mostly steady, with only a few isolated alerts interrupting routine maintenance. Outside of a scheduled exercise mid-week, our core booking flows remained stable across all regions. The issues encountered were driven either by partner traffic spikes or third-party upstream latency rather than internal release regressions.

## 2. What happened

A detailed rundown of the events and operational tasks recorded during this shift:

* On Tuesday 2026-02-17 at 10:33 JST, the alert api-partner-reject fired for one partner. Looking into the traffic in sorrel-prod-* showed that the partner ran a full re-sync and hit its contracted limit. The first move was to read logs to see the volume and verify which partner was making the requests. I followed up internally with the service owner, and Ravi confirmed the limit stays as it is, so no throttling parameters were altered.

* Later that evening, on Tuesday 2026-02-17 at 20:30 JST, the payments-provider-timeout fired. The first move was check provider; the stripe status page reported degraded API performance on their end. The incident cleared in 24 minutes without requiring intervention on our side.

* We had a planned game day on Thursday 2026-02-19: we moved api traffic out of eu-west (a region evacuation) and back. Sara ran it; the evacuation took 41 minutes end to end, against a target of 30. We collected metrics on routing latency and drain times during the shift. Follow-up tickets are with Ravi to address the bottlenecks that kept us from hitting the thirty-minute window.

* Additionally, I spent time watching operational dashboards during regular peak hours. A known dashboard behavior stood out during evening notifications: the queue depth panel on the 'Sorrel / notifier' board lags the delivered-per-minute panel by about 2 minutes; read both before deciding when evaluating delivery backlogs.

## 3. Service status

* web: Normal; no operational issues or paging events recorded during the week.
* api: Normal; see the partner re-sync on Tuesday and the planned eu-west evacuation on Thursday.
* payments: Normal; see the upstream Stripe latency on Tuesday evening.
* notifier: Normal; delivery processing remained healthy throughout the shift.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

* Keep an eye on api-partner-reject if third parties retry bulk jobs during working hours. Remember that partner limits remain firm per Ravi, so check the log search tool to confirm request volume before taking any other steps.
* The eu-west evacuation showed where our drain process spends the extra 11 minutes. Since Sara ran it, she is already familiar with the flow, but Ravi holds the follow-up tickets for tightening the evacuation timeline.
* When inspecting messaging queues, remember the quirk noted above: the queue depth panel on the 'Sorrel / notifier' board lags the delivered-per-minute panel by about 2 minutes; read both before deciding whether notifier is actually backing up.
* Upstream card provider performance is clean right now, but standard procedure applies if timeouts resurface: verify their public dashboard immediately.
* Handover will be complete once Sara acknowledges this log and writes "taken" in #inc-live.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the rotation to Sara for the upcoming week. The boards and logs are clear heading into Monday morning.

— Daniel

You write internal pages for the SRE team of Sorrel. Write ONE page in Markdown, plain and realistic,
the way a small, busy SRE team writes: specific, a little dry, short sections, bullets where they help, no marketing
tone, no summary of what the page is for. Length: 550 to 700 words; do not stop short.
Sections, in this order, with numbered '## ' headings in the house style ('## 1. Shift summary'):
shift summary (two or three sentences, the author's view of the week); what happened (each fact, with the author's
plain account of what was seen and done); a one-line-per-service status for web, api, payments and notifier (normal,
or pointing back to what happened; no new numbers); notes for the incoming on-call; sign-off.

Start with exactly the header lines you are given, unchanged. Then write the body.

Hard rules:
- Use every fact you are given, with every number, name, code, config key and date exactly as written. Add no new
  facts: no new incidents, numbers, error codes, config keys, partner names or people. You may add connecting words,
  a one-line judgement from the author, and a routine sign-off.
- Keep the team's own words for things exactly as the facts give them; do not explain a term in other words and do not
  add a plain-language gloss.
- An error code (like ABC-1234) appears only where a fact puts it, written in passing inside a sentence. Never put an
  error code in a heading, a table header or the first line of a section.
- Never give rollback steps or rollback commands for any service. Never mention a tool called dtool. Mention Shipyard
  only if a fact does, and then only as the fact says, with no commands.
- No phone numbers, account ids, email addresses or URLs. Do not mention on-call pay, allowances or contracts.
- Do not copy alert rules or thresholds into tables, and do not write lists of 'for this alert, the first move is X'.
- Everything in the page happens on or before the page's date.

What the team works with:
Sorrel is a scheduling app (salons, clinics, tutors book appointments through it). Four services: web
(pages and the admin tool), api (businesses, bookings, search, the partner API, the audit log), payments (charges,
refunds, weekly payouts to businesses), notifier (email and SMS). Regions: ap-northeast, us-east, eu-west.
Owners: Aiko (web), Ravi (api), Mei (payments), Tom (notifier). Others: Kenji Sato (platform lead), Sara (platform
engineer), Hana (support lead), Daniel (api engineer), Yuki (notifier engineer), Priya (web engineer), Leo (payments
engineer), Noor (SRE, joined the rotation in April 2026). Providers: stripe (cards), twilio (SMS), sendgrid (email),
cloudflare (CDN and firewall), aws (hosting). The incident channel is #inc-live; boards are "Sorrel / web",
"Sorrel / api", "Sorrel / payments", "Sorrel / notifier"; logs are searched in sorrel-prod-*; people use the paging
tool, the metrics tool, the log search tool and the deploy tool. Severities: P1, P2, P3. A handover is finished when
the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

The five actions on-call chooses from:
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

# On-call handover, week of 2026-03-09

Date: 2026-03-09  
Owner: Priya (web), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Leo (payments)  

## 1. Shift summary

A fairly steady shift overall, though stripe gave us two noisy stretches mid-week that tested our ingest boundaries. Downstream services held up as expected under the replay pressure, and partner traffic over the weekend produced one limit alert that turned out to be expected partner behavior. Routine deploys went out during our scheduled windows without incident.

## 2. What happened

The notable events during this rotation:

- Webhook replay storm on Tuesday: after stripe's incident cleared, stripe re-sent about 48,000 old events in 20 minutes. payments-webhook-retry fired; the events are deduplicated by event id, so we let it drain (about 35 minutes). No action needed beyond the log line.
- payments-provider-timeout fired on Wednesday 2026-03-04 at 20:25 JST; the stripe status page reported degraded API performance; cleared in 29 minutes. First move: check provider. The delay resided outside our stack, and upstream recovery cleared the alert state cleanly once requests went through without timing out.
- api-partner-reject fired for one partner on Saturday 2026-03-07 at 10:57 JST: the partner ran a full re-sync and hit its contracted limit. Ravi confirmed the limit stays as it is. First move: read logs. Once we verified the log output showed standard quota rejections rather than unexpected gateway failures, we closed the loop with Ravi and took no further intervention.
- Deploys this week: web 2, api 1, payments 1, notifier 1; all in the Tuesday and Thursday afternoon windows. None of the releases required follow-up patches, and all services remained stable across all regions throughout each rollout.

## 3. Service status

- web: normal, stable following the two scheduled rollouts.
- api: normal, pointing back to the partner limit rejection on Saturday.
- payments: normal, pointing back to the webhook storm and stripe provider degradation.
- notifier: normal, no alerts or delivery issues recorded this week.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- Watch stripe ingest behavior closely if upstream reports any residual maintenance; Tuesday showed that when stripe flushes backlogged webhooks, the payments ingestion queue will spike significantly, though deduplication protects underlying balance records.
- Keep in mind that when api-partner-reject fires, checking the partner's historical synchronization patterns is helpful before reaching out to engineering owners; Ravi's stance on contracted quotas remains strict.
- Deployment schedules remain locked to the regular Tuesday and Thursday afternoon slots; all changes across the four services are currently in sync with production baselines.
- For provider-related hiccups, verifying external status dashboards early prevents needless deep dives into local application telemetry.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the rotation to Leo. Please review the notes above, verify dashboard baselines across the services, and post taken in #inc-live once you have assumed primary coverage for the coming shift.

# On-call handover, week of 2026-03-23

Date: 2026-03-23  
Owner: Yuki (notifier), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Daniel (api)  

## 1. Shift summary

The week was mostly quiet, with no major internal service faults or Sev incidents opened in #inc-live. Our only pages were short-lived blips originating from external partners, both of which cleared without engineering intervention. Overall delivery across our primary pipelines remained steady, and the planned partner API deprecation went through smoothly on Wednesday.

## 2. What happened

- On Tuesday 2026-03-17, notifier-sms-fail fired for 7 minutes. Looked into delivery metrics for SMS and saw downstream drops across ap-northeast. The twilio status page listed a carrier incident in Japan; delivery recovered on its own. First move: check provider. Since this cleared naturally once upstream routing recovered, no further changes were needed on our side.
- On Wednesday 2026-03-18, the old v1 partner API endpoints were switched off, after the last partner moved to v2. About 3 calls a day still arrive on v1 from a test script at Hanabi Booking; they get 410 and Ravi has told them. - On Friday 2026-03-20, web-cdn-edge reached 2.4 % for 6 minutes. The cloudflare status page showed an incident at one edge location. First move: check provider. ## 3. Service status

- web: Normal; briefly saw web-cdn-edge reached 2.4 % for 6 minutes on Friday due to upstream CDN issues, now clear.

- payments: Normal; no alerts fired and processing remained stable across all regions throughout the rotation.
- notifier: Normal; briefly had notifier-sms-fail fired for 7 minutes on Tuesday due to carrier issues in Japan, now fully clear.

- Quirk: the log search tool's default time window is the last 15 minutes; widen it before deciding there are no errors. When hunting down intermittent issues or checking up on trailing alerts across sorrel-prod-*, make sure you adjust that range first so you do not miss context from earlier in the hour.
- Watch out for residual pings from Hanabi Booking hitting v1 on api. As noted, Ravi has reached out, so if you happen to spot those in the audit log or route metrics, do not spend time chasing them down as regressions.
- If third-party edge or provider delivery alerts trigger again, check their respective status dashboards before digging into our own configurations.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the primary rotation to Daniel. Please check your notifications in the paging tool and post "taken" in #inc-live once you have completed your review of this page and the active monitoring boards.

— Yuki

Author: Daniel (api), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Leo (payments)  

## 1. Shift summary

The past week was generally quiet across all core application services without any major internal regressions. System health across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west returned to baseline quickly in each instance without requiring service restarts or emergency interventions.

The cloudflare status page showed an incident at one edge location, explaining the brief drop in availability before edge routing stabilized. The event resolved itself promptly once upstream transit normalized, without spreading errors to our origin instances.

No other alerts paged during the shift, and neither event required escalating to a P1 or waking secondary engineers outside normal working hours.

## 3. Service status

- web: Normal, recovering cleanly following the brief cloudflare edge elevation on Thursday 2026-03-26.
- api: Normal across all regions, with steady performance on booking and partner endpoints.
- payments: Normal throughout the week, with regular charge execution and routine payout runs completed without issues.
- notifier: Normal, operating cleanly after the temporary sendgrid delay observed on Wednesday 2026-03-25.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- Reminder for incoming: no deploys after 16:00 JST on Friday or between 22:00 and 07:00 JST, except rollbacks and fixes for open P1s.
- Keep an eye on external partner boards and status dashboards whenever edge or notification alerts trigger before attempting origin-side mitigations.
- Ensure all regional clusters remain balanced across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west during scheduled application updates via the deploy tool.
- Check the log search tool if any sporadic queue spikes appear in notifier or payments workers during off-peak hours.
- A handover is finished when the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing off primary coverage to Leo for the coming week.

Daniel (api)

Date: 2026-04-13  
Owner: Daniel (api), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Sara (platform)  

## 1. Shift summary

The rotation was mostly quiet this week with two minor alerts and clean scheduled background work. Neither page required waking a service owner or escalating to a formal incident, and customer traffic was unaffected. Overall the platform behaved predictably across all three regions.

## 2. What happened

On Wednesday 2026-04-08, web-disk passed 80 % on one web node because of old log files. The initial move was to read logs to see what was consuming capacity on the host. Once the cause was verified as stale retained output rather than runaway growth from active processes, Priya cleared the rotated logs in working hours. No further disk space alarms triggered on that host or across the rest of the pool after the cleanup.

Over the weekend, notifier-queue-depth fired at Saturday 2026-04-11 03:54 JST during the nightly reminder batch in ap-northeast (peak 1070 messages). The backlog accumulated briefly while customer reminder dispatches went out in bulk. The chosen move was no action, as delivered per minute stayed normal and the queue drained before 05:00 without dropping messages or stalling downstream workers.

On Sunday night, the regular scheduled payments batch ran as planned. The Sunday payout job ran at 23:00 JST and finished in 42 minutes, processing all weekly disbursements to businesses cleanly with no failures reported by the payments service or the provider.

## 3. Service status

- web: Normal; recovered after Priya cleared the rotated logs on the node that hit the disk threshold on Wednesday.
- api: Normal; ran without alerts, elevated error rates, or queue delays throughout the shift.
- payments: Normal; the Sunday payout job completed without issues during its late run.
- notifier: Normal; queue drained before 05:00 following the brief reminder batch spike in ap-northeast on Saturday.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- The web host that alerted on Wednesday is back down well below alert levels, but keep an eye on log rotation across the web instances if disk warnings surface again.

- The payments payout completed its full cycle cleanly, so no stranded batch states or reconciliation tickets are pending for Monday morning.
- Normal operational checks remain standard across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over the primary rotation to Sara. Please acknowledge and mark the rotation as taken in #inc-live once ready.

— Daniel

# On-call handover, week of 2026-04-20

Last updated: 2026-04-20 10:00 JST  
Owner: Sara (platform), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Priya (web)  

## 1. Shift summary

The shift was mostly quiet, with no major pages overnight and standard baseline traffic across all three regions. Noor shadowed Sara all week: her first shadow shift. Most of our operational work went into tracking down a delayed booking cleanup issue and watching edge metrics during a brief third-party blip on Friday.

## 2. What happened

A couple of specific items came up through the week that required investigation or team follow-up:

* **Orphaned holds on booking slots**: When a customer leaves checkout, the slot should be released after 10 minutes, but the hold reaper job had been paused since the api deploy on 2026-04-14, so abandoned slots stayed held until the 30-minute safety timeout and showed as taken. This led to extra capacity being tied up longer than expected across businesses during peak scheduling hours. We walked through the reaper process during our shift, and Ravi restarted the reaper on Friday. Once the job was running again, the backlog of abandoned checkouts cleared down to normal levels and slots began releasing on the standard schedule.
* **Edge error blip**: On Friday 2026-04-17, web-cdn-edge reached 2.3 % for 6 minutes. When the spike appeared in the metrics tool, the team chose to check provider as the immediate step. The cloudflare status page showed an incident at one edge location. No origin changes were made from our side, and error rates dropped back under threshold as the provider resolved the localized issue on their network. First move: check provider.

## 3. Service status

* **web**: Normal; edge blip on Friday 2026-04-17 resolved once the provider cleared their edge location issue.
* **api**: Normal; holding behavior returned to expected release intervals after Ravi restarted the reaper on Friday.
* **payments**: Normal; charges, refunds, and payouts processed cleanly throughout the shift.
* **notifier**: Normal; message delivery queues remained within normal boundaries across all regions.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

* Noor completed her first shadow shift with Sara; she is familiar with the paging tool and our dashboard layout, but keep her looped into any non-trivial investigations this week.
* Keep an eye on hold reaper metrics on the "Sorrel / api" board early in the week to verify the job continues to sweep abandoned checkout holds at the 10-minute mark rather than drifting toward the safety timeout again.
* If edge errors elevate on web surfaces, remember to check provider before looking at origin health or local container states.
* Reminder for incoming: no deploys after 16:00 JST on Friday or between 22:00 and 07:00 JST, except rollbacks and fixes for open P1s. Make sure engineers scheduling release trains in the deploy tool adhere strictly to these cutoffs unless an active incident requires an emergency patch.
* Regular logs remain accessible across sorrel-prod-* clusters if you need to trace individual booking or checkout flows.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over primary rotation duties to Priya. Handover completes when Priya acknowledges and writes "taken" in #inc-live.

— Sara

parts.text:
You write internal pages for the SRE team of Sorrel. Write ONE page in Markdown, plain and realistic,
the way a small, busy SRE team writes: specific, a little dry, short sections, bullets where they help, no marketing
tone, no summary of what the page is for. Length: 550 to 700 words; do not stop short.
Sections, in this order, with numbered '## ' headings in the house style ('## 1. Shift summary'):
shift summary (two or three sentences, the author's view of the week); what happened (each fact, with the author's
plain account of what was seen and done); a one-line-per-service status for web, api, payments and notifier (normal,
or pointing back to what happened; no new numbers); notes for the incoming on-call; sign-off.

Start with exactly the header lines you are given, unchanged. Then write the body.

Hard rules:
- Use every fact you are given, with every number, name, code, config key and date exactly as written. Add no new
  facts: no new incidents, numbers, error codes, config keys, partner names or people. You may add connecting words,
  a one-line judgement from the author, and a routine sign-off.
- Keep the team's own words for things exactly as the facts give them; do not explain a term in other words and do not
  add a plain-language gloss.
- An error code (like ABC-1234) appears only where a fact puts it, written in passing inside a sentence. Never put an
  error code in a heading, a table header or the first line of a section.
- Never give rollback steps or rollback commands for any service. Never mention a tool called dtool. Mention Shipyard
  only if a fact does, and then only as the fact says, with no commands.
- No phone numbers, account ids, email addresses or URLs. Do not mention on-call pay, allowances or contracts.
- Do not copy alert rules or thresholds into tables, and do not write lists of 'for this alert, the first move is X'.
- Everything in the page happens on or before the page's date.

What the team works with:
Sorrel is a scheduling app (salons, clinics, tutors book appointments through it). Four services: web
(pages and the admin tool), api (businesses, bookings, search, the partner API, the audit log), payments (charges,
refunds, weekly payouts to businesses), notifier (email and SMS). Regions: ap-northeast, us-east, eu-west.
Owners: Aiko (web), Ravi (api), Mei (payments), Tom (notifier). Others: Kenji Sato (platform lead), Sara (platform
engineer), Hana (support lead), Daniel (api engineer), Yuki (notifier engineer), Priya (web engineer), Leo (payments
engineer), Noor (SRE, joined the rotation in April 2026). Providers: stripe (cards), twilio (SMS), sendgrid (email),
cloudflare (CDN and firewall), aws (hosting). The incident channel is #inc-live; boards are "Sorrel / web",
"Sorrel / api", "Sorrel / payments", "Sorrel / notifier"; logs are searched in sorrel-prod-*; people use the paging
tool, the metrics tool, the log search tool and the deploy tool. Severities: P1, P2, P3. A handover is finished when
the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

The five actions on-call chooses from:
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

- Deploys this week: web 2, api 2, payments 1, notifier 1; all in the Tuesday and Thursday afternoon windows. Each release completed without causing elevation in baseline metrics, and no hotfixes were introduced.

- web: normal, aside from the brief cloudflare edge elevation on Thursday 2026-05-14.
- api: normal throughout the entire shift with clean deployment runs and steady latency.

- Query volume across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west has remained balanced, and log checks in sorrel-prod-* show clean traces outside of the upstream events noted above.

Handing over the primary pager now. The shift is ready for transfer whenever you are set to acknowledge it.

Please reply when ready; this handover is finished when the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

— Noor

Author: Noor (SRE), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Priya (web)  

## 1. Shift summary

The rotation was mostly quiet this week with low operational drag across all primary regions. We dealt with a background job fix for large admin exports, one routine disk cleanup, and a standard nightly queue surge in Tokyo that resolved on its own. Support had no critical customer escalations for us, leaving platform traffic stable through the weekend.

## 2. What happened

- On Wednesday 2026-05-27 at 03:18 JST, the alert notifier-queue-depth fired during the nightly reminder batch in ap-northeast. The backlog reached a peak of 1140 messages. Aiko's team changed large exports to run in the background and show up in the admin tool's downloads list when ready; shipped Thursday. The fix landed cleanly and the timeout has not reappeared since.

- Later in the week, web-disk passed 80 % on one web node on Friday 2026-05-29 because of old log files. Priya cleared the rotated logs in working hours, bringing disk headroom back well under threshold. First move: read logs.

- Support (Hana) had a quiet week: no escalations to on-call. Ticket volume stayed within their tier-one handling capacity, and no customer reports required triage or off-hours intervention from the platform side.

## 3. Service status

- web: Degraded earlier in the week due to the export timeout and log accumulation on one box, now fully normal following the background export release and disk cleanup.

- payments: Normal across all processing pipelines, batch payout cycles, and ledger checks.
- notifier: Normal; queue drained before 05:00 after the ap-northeast nightly reminder run described above.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- The background job pattern for admin tool downloads shipped by Aiko's team on Thursday is now handling heavy data sets. Keep half an eye on the admin tool worker pools if support requests further massive booking dumps, though early metrics look healthy.
- The web tier disk cleanup on Friday was handled manually during business hours. While capacity is fine right now, it is worth checking the log rotation behavior on the remaining web instances if disk alerts pop up again.
- Reminder queue behavior in ap-northeast will likely spike similarly around 03:00 JST during nightly batches, but as long as delivery throughput remains steady, it does not require intervention.
- The rotation transfer will formally complete once Priya posts the standard confirmation.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over primary on-call duty to Priya for the coming week. Please remember to post "taken" in #inc-live to finalize the rotation transfer.

# On-call handover, week of 2026-06-15

Last updated: 2026-06-15 10:00 JST  
Owner: Leo (payments), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Yuki (notifier)  

## 1. Shift summary

The shift was mostly quiet, with only two alerts firing during the week. Both events resolved cleanly without any service degradation on our end, though one required watching an upstream vendor during off-hours. Overall, core systems remained stable across the rotation and no customer-facing failures occurred.

## 2. What happened

Two alerts fired across the week:

* On Wednesday 2026-06-10 at 20:18 JST, `payments-provider-timeout` fired. The alert pointed directly at external processing, so the first move was check provider. The stripe status page reported degraded API performance; cleared in 27 minutes. No further intervention was needed once upstream latency subsided, and the alert recovered on its own without manual intervention on the payments service.
* On Friday 2026-06-12 at 14:52 JST, `web-traffic` fired. A quick check of traffic showed a search-engine crawler on public business pages, about 3.2x the same hour last week, all 2xx. * web: Normal, apart from the crawler surge mentioned under what happened.
* api: Normal throughout the week with no alerts firing.
* payments: Normal; the brief timeout spike followed the stripe degradation noted above.
* notifier: Normal across the entire shift with clean dispatch queues.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

* Quirk: the queue depth panel on the 'Sorrel / notifier' board lags the delivered-per-minute panel by about 2 minutes; read both before deciding.

* The crawler ticket for Aiko remains open for web, so keep an eye out if public page crawling spikes again before limits are adjusted.
* General system health looks clean heading into the week, with standard load patterns across the regions and no unresolved active pages left hanging from the previous rotation.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over primary duty now. Please post in #inc-live once you have reviewed the boards and taken the shift.

— Leo

# On-call handover, week of 2026-06-22

Last updated: 2026-06-22 10:00 JST  
Owner: Yuki (notifier), outgoing on-call  
Incoming on-call: Daniel (api)  

## 1. Shift summary

A fairly calm week with only a couple of minor alerts across web, both resolved quickly without widespread customer impact. The scheduled weekly batch tasks completed cleanly without incident, and no P1 or P2 severities were declared. Most routine SRE attention was spent observing edge traffic and a node replacement in us-east.

## 2. What happened

- On Tuesday 2026-06-16, `web.session_idle_minutes` went from 30 to 60. Support asked for this change because businesses were being signed out of the booking screen in the middle of the day. Aiko approved the change before it was applied, and we have had no further complaints regarding premature sign-outs from clinic or salon staff.
- Also on Tuesday 2026-06-16, `web-node-restart` fired for one us-east web node following two restarts in 30 minutes due to running out of memory. First move: read logs. The logs confirmed the process was running out of memory, and the node was replaced. The replacement host came up clean and memory usage across us-east has remained stable since.
- On Wednesday 2026-06-17, `web-4xx` sat at 1.5 % for 12 minutes. First move: read logs. Inspection showed the brief elevation was caused by an old marketing link pointing at a removed page rather than broken navigation inside the app. There were no customer reports, and a ticket was filed with the marketing team to clean up the external redirect.
- On Sunday 2026-06-21, the Sunday payout job ran at 23:00 JST and finished in 41 minutes. All batches processed without failures or retries.

## 3. Service status

- **web**: Normal, following the single node replacement in us-east and the updated session idle setting.
- **api**: Normal, quiet throughout the week with no alerts or disruptions.
- **payments**: Normal, Sunday payout job ran at 23:00 JST and finished in 41 minutes.
- **notifier**: Normal, no delivery backlogs or provider warnings across email or SMS.

## 4. Notes for the incoming on-call

- Keep an eye on memory across the web fleet in us-east after Tuesday's single node replacement, though sorrel-prod-* logs have shown no recurring leaks or further restarts since the instance was swapped out.
- The change to `web.session_idle_minutes` from 30 to 60 has eliminated midday disconnections for businesses, but watch for any unexpected session store bloat on web.
- The ticket filed for the dead marketing URL generating the 4xx blip is tracked on the web board if follow-up is needed during business hours.
- Regular traffic patterns remain standard across ap-northeast, us-east, and eu-west. Paging tools and alert states are currently all green.

## 5. Sign-off

Handing over primary rotation now. Daniel, please review the notes and post "taken" in #inc-live to complete the handover.

— Yuki

You write internal pages for the SRE team of Sorrel. Write ONE page in Markdown, plain and realistic,
the way a small, busy SRE team writes: specific, a little dry, short sections, bullets where they help, no marketing
tone, no summary of what the page is for. Length: 550 to 700 words; do not stop short.
Sections, in this order, with numbered '## ' headings in the house style ('## 1. Shift summary'):
shift summary (two or three sentences, the author's view of the week); what happened (each fact, with the author's
plain account of what was seen and done); a one-line-per-service status for web, api, payments and notifier (normal,
or pointing back to what happened; no new numbers); notes for the incoming on-call; sign-off.

Start with exactly the header lines you are given, unchanged. Then write the body.

Hard rules:
- Use every fact you are given, with every number, name, code, config key and date exactly as written. Add no new
  facts: no new incidents, numbers, error codes, config keys, partner names or people. You may add connecting words,
  a one-line judgement from the author, and a routine sign-off.
- Keep the team's own words for things exactly as the facts give them; do not explain a term in other words and do not
  add a plain-language gloss.
- An error code (like ABC-1234) appears only where a fact puts it, written in passing inside a sentence. Never put an
  error code in a heading, a table header or the first line of a section.
- Never give rollback steps or rollback commands for any service. Never mention a tool called dtool. Mention Shipyard
  only if a fact does, and then only as the fact says, with no commands.
- No phone numbers, account ids, email addresses or URLs. Do not mention on-call pay, allowances or contracts.
- Do not copy alert rules or thresholds into tables, and do not write lists of 'for this alert, the first move is X'.
- Everything in the page happens on or before the page's date.

What the team works with:
Sorrel is a scheduling app (salons, clinics, tutors book appointments through it). Four services: web
(pages and the admin tool), api (businesses, bookings, search, the partner API, the audit log), payments (charges,
refunds, weekly payouts to businesses), notifier (email and SMS). Regions: ap-northeast, us-east, eu-west.
Owners: Aiko (web), Ravi (api), Mei (payments), Tom (notifier). Others: Kenji Sato (platform lead), Sara (platform
engineer), Hana (support lead), Daniel (api engineer), Yuki (notifier engineer), Priya (web engineer), Leo (payments
engineer), Noor (SRE, joined the rotation in April 2026). Providers: stripe (cards), twilio (SMS), sendgrid (email),
cloudflare (CDN and firewall), aws (hosting). The incident channel is #inc-live; boards are "Sorrel / web",
"Sorrel / api", "Sorrel / payments", "Sorrel / notifier"; logs are searched in sorrel-prod-*; people use the paging
tool, the metrics tool, the log search tool and the deploy tool. Severities: P1, P2, P3. A handover is finished when
the incoming on-call writes "taken" in #inc-live.

The five actions on-call chooses from:
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

Author: Sara (platform), outgoing on-call
